description: A mobile app that displays the users current GPS location and then looks up the nearest tides, wind speed and wind direction for that location using public weather APIs.
longDescription:
The UI should have a single comprehensive page similar to Apples Weather app but instead of weather, it shows GPS location, time of day with a time slider to adjust the current time, and then a graphic chart of the plus/minus/average tides for that location.  Positive tides are black filled area under the graph line, while negative tides are filled with red under the graph line.   The actual tide value is displayed and updates as the slider is moved.   The display should be gentle, clean and balanced.   Fonts should be artistic (not monospaced).  The splash page should have just a brief shot of a tide scene with the Tide Tracker name prominently displayed, then fade out to the graphic display.   There should be a Settings page where the user can tweak things like meters vs feet,  AM/PM versus 24 hour clock, etc. etc.   When the app quits, the settings are saved and reloaded on next launch.   

There should be a report of the average wind speed and direction at the top of the graphic display which updates for the time selected on the time slider.    

Use public weather and tide APIs to pull the data and live update the graphic display on the main view

Winds above a certain threshhold speed (chosen by the user in the Settings) should be displayed in a contrasting color to illustrate a high winds situation.
intendedAudience: Recreational boaters, kayakers, paddle board users, beachcombers, and those who plan to be out on the water and need to know when the tide or wind will change that day.

projectRules:
- All temporary or persistent data that is stored locally should be formatted and written to disk as JSON with the goal to be compatible with MongoDB.   The goal is to have seamless migration to MongoDB remote backing store when that feature is implemented.
- Before adding a feature, search the codebase for an existing implementation that already solves the same problem (or most of it) to prevent, if possible, one-off solutions eventually bloating the code base.
- Design modular code.  Use class and sublasses as much as possible to encapsulate behaviors to avoid creating one-off solutions to common or similar problems. Child classes should extend parent classes rather than be created de novo to solve a new request.
- You can respond to a prompt by asking if an existing class should be used and/or extended before writing new code to solve a problem.  
- Keep code organized and well documented. 
- Remove abandoned, unused, or non-functioning code.  
- New classes custom to my project should use a prefix for namespacing, such as 'Themed'.   For example a styled button unique to my project would then be named 'ThemedStyledButton'
- BIYcoder Astro workspaces use a **scaffolded CSS framework** (Bootstrap, Bulma, etc.) wired through `src/styles/global.css`. That file imports the vendor bundle from `node_modules` and then `./biycoder-theme-overrides.css`.  Styles that modify or update the scaffolded CSS framework are to be stored in the overrides.css file and no changes are to be made to the node_modules files.
- Respect a common color style and theme for UI across visible user elements. Keep one look and global style for the entire project.    Utilize the 'overrides.css' to make changes to the base style.  Apply the same styling to elements that are used in different views of the project.   For example, all listboxes should look the same, all tabpanels should keep the same styling, etc.   Buttons of the same importance have the same default styling unless specifically asked to modify.
-
Site styling uses Pure.css (pure_css). Change appearance only in src/styles/biycoder-theme-overrides.css. Never edit node_modules. Pure has minimal theming; set base colors on body, a, and .pure-button-primary in overrides.
postScaffoldAgentPrompt:
Scaffold a new Astro project workspace with the following specifications. Follow each section precisely when generating pages, layout, styling, routes, and shared site chrome.

## Getting Started

Project name: Wind Tide Tracker
Project slug: wind-tide-tracker (permanent lowercase folder id for the workspace on disk)
Build type: PWA
Build targets (responsive layouts for): Phone, Tablet.

## Concept

General Description:
A mobile app that displays the users current GPS location and then looks up the nearest tides, wind speed and wind direction for that location using public weather APIs.

Unique Features:
The UI should have a single comprehensive page similar to Apples Weather app but instead of weather, it shows GPS location, time of day with a time slider to adjust the current time, and then a graphic chart of the plus/minus/average tides for that location.  Positive tides are black filled area under the graph line, while negative tides are filled with red under the graph line.   The actual tide value is displayed and updates as the slider is moved.   The display should be gentle, clean and balanced.   Fonts should be artistic (not monospaced).  The splash page should have just a brief shot of a tide scene with the Tide Tracker name prominently displayed, then fade out to the graphic display.   There should be a Settings page where the user can tweak things like meters vs feet,  AM/PM versus 24 hour clock, etc. etc.   When the app quits, the settings are saved and reloaded on next launch.   

There should be a report of the average wind speed and direction at the top of the graphic display which updates for the time selected on the time slider.    

Use public weather and tide APIs to pull the data and live update the graphic display on the main view

Winds above a certain threshhold speed (chosen by the user in the Settings) should be displayed in a contrasting color to illustrate a high winds situation.

Intended Audience and Uses:
Recreational boaters, kayakers, paddle board users, beachcombers, and those who plan to be out on the water and need to know when the tide or wind will change that day.

## Key Features and Initial Views

Scaffold these key features into the site layout and shared chrome:
- Splash Screen: Full-screen intro for a second or two while the app or site loads.
- Top Menu Bar for Tablet layout: Primary navigation links across the top of every page.
- Mobile Menu (Hamburger Menu): Collapsible navigation for small screens and touch devices.

Create these initial Astro views as routable pages:
- Home → / (home page at src/pages/index.astro)
- About → /about (src/pages/about.astro)
- Settings → /settings (src/pages/settings.astro)
- Help → /help (src/pages/help.astro)
- FAQ → /faq (src/pages/faq.astro)
- Tides Display → /tides-display (src/pages/tides-display.astro)

## Styling and Icons

CSS framework: Pure.css
Site styling uses Pure.css (pure_css). Change appearance only in src/styles/biycoder-theme-overrides.css. Never edit node_modules. Pure has minimal theming; set base colors on body, a, and .pure-button-primary in overrides.

Icon library: Google Material Symbols
Use the Google Material Symbols icon library consistently across all pages.
